Aker Solutions ASA Reports Steady Revenue Growth in Q1 Amid Robust North Sea Activity

Aker Solutions ASA posted a solid set of first-quarter results on Wednesday, highlighting steady revenue growth and resilient order intake against a backdrop of continued investment in Norway’s offshore oil and gas sector.

The Oslo-based oilfield services provider reported revenues of NOK 9.3 billion for the first quarter, up 6% from NOK 8.8 billion in the same period last year. Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) rose to NOK 512 million, compared to NOK 483 million a year earlier. Net profit for the three months ended March 31 stood at NOK 328 million, up from NOK 307 million.

Order intake remained robust, with Aker Solutions ASA securing new contracts valued at NOK 10.1 billion, driven primarily by subsea and engineering projects on the Norwegian continental shelf. The company’s order backlog reached NOK 52.4 billion at quarter-end, providing healthy visibility for the remainder of the year.

“Our performance in the first quarter reflects strong project execution and ongoing demand for our expertise in complex offshore developments,” said CEO Ingrid Johansen. “We continue to see high activity levels in the North Sea, and our focus on digitalization and sustainability is driving efficiency across our operations.”

Analysts noted that Aker Solutions ASA’s results slightly exceeded consensus expectations, buoyed by higher project margins and stable costs. “Aker Solutions is benefiting from the sustained investment by operators in Norway, as well as disciplined cost control,” commented Lars Eide, energy sector analyst at Nordvest Securities. “The company’s backlog and contract wins position it well for the coming quarters.”

The company reaffirmed its full-year outlook, projecting mid-single-digit revenue growth and stable margins. Capital expenditure for the year remains unchanged at around NOK 650 million.

Aker Solutions ASA shares rose 2.1% in early trading on the Oslo Stock Exchange following the results announcement. The company employs approximately 14,500 people globally, with a significant presence in Stavanger, Bergen, and Trondheim.
